The proof of the theorem `lg_target` relies on the fact that the product of elements modulo `n` is preserved when each element is congruent modulo `n`. This can be shown using the lemma `SModEq.prod`, which states that if two functions `f` and `g` are congruent modulo an ideal (in this case, the ideal generated by `n` in the ring of integers), then their products over a finite set are also congruent modulo that ideal.

Since `f x ≡ g x [MOD n]` for all `x ∈ s`, it follows that `f x - g x` is divisible by `n` for each such `x`. Therefore, the product of `f x` over `s` differs from the product of `g x` over `s` by a multiple of `n`, which implies that the two products are congruent modulo `n`. Thus, the theorem follows directly from the lemma `SModEq.prod`.
